chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Can the one in Ihram veil himself from the sun?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if he is an old man.' Or he said: '(If he is) with an illness.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: the one in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram cover their head from the sun?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the general prohibition against covering the head for the sake of the sun remains, it is lifted for the elderly or those with specific ailments (*dhawu 'illatin*), reflecting the principle of *rukhsah* (concession) in Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the balance between maintaining the sanctity of Ihram and preventing undue hardship, a key theme in Ja'fari jurisprudence.
